report:
Prikazane koštane strukture su primjerenih intenziteta signala, primjerene morfologije.
Zglobna tijela su kongruentna. Kut lateralne trohlearne inklinacije iznosi 11°.
Patella alta - Insall Salvati index 1,4.
Hondromalacija patelarne hrskavice III°.
Hondromalacija I° kondilarne i tibijalne hrskavice medijalnog kompartmenta.
Križni ligamenti održanog tijeka, primjerenih intenziteta signala.
Ne nalazi se znakova osteohondralne lezije.
Menisci su primjerenih intenziteta signala i morfologije.
Kolateralni ligamenti su održanog tijeka, primjerenih intenziteta signala.
Prikazane mišićno-tetivne strukture primjerenog prikaza.
Bez izljeva u zglobni prostor.

Findings:  There is a complex tear of the anterior horn of the medial meniscus at the junction with the meniscal body with a radial and horizontal component extending to involve the meniscal body. The lateral meniscus is intact with no displaced or flipped fragments.  There is a full-thickness tear of the ACL with the resultant buckling of the PCL and anterior tibial translation. The PCL remains intact.  Intact MCL. The lateral collateral ligament complex including the popliteus tendon, popliteofibular and distal biceps tendon are intact. There is a grade 1 injury of the popliteus musculotendinous complex.  No chondral injury. No sinister bone marrow signal. Small joint effusion with a small amount of fluid within the medial gastrocnemius semimembranosus bursa.  
Impression:  Full-thickness ACL tear. Complex tear of the medial meniscus with a radial and horizontal component.

Exam Type: MRI KNEE RIGHT WO CONTRAST
Exam Date and Time: [DATE] [TIME]
Indication: Right knee pain, soccer injury.
Comparison: [REDACTED].

TECHNIQUE:
MRI of the right knee was performed on a 1.5 Tesla system with a dedicated knee coil in three planes (axial, sagittal, and coronal), using a standard non-contrast protocol.

FINDINGS:
OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:
Alignment is anatomic. Osseous contusion at the posterior lateral tibial plateau with minimal residual osseous contusion at the periphery of the medial femoral condyle and lateral femoral condyle. Background marrow signal is normal without infiltrative marrow process. No aggressive osseous lesions.

JOINT SPACE:
Moderate joint effusion. Focal nodular synovial proliferation at the anterior joint line. No intra-articular bodies. No Baker's cyst.

MEDIAL COMPARTMENT:
Medial meniscus: Normal in morphology and signal.
Medial compartment cartilage: No focal cartilage defects.

LATERAL COMPARTMENT:
Lateral meniscus: Horizontal tear in the posterior body and posterior horn of the medial meniscus. No extrusion. No displaced fragments.
Lateral compartment cartilage: High-grade cartilage loss along the posterior lateral tibial plateau.

PATELLOFEMORAL COMPARTMENT:
Patellofemoral compartment cartilage: Low-grade chondral fraying along the medial and lateral patellar facet.

CRUCIATE LIGAMENTS:
Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL): Complete subacute tear of the ACL.
Posterior cruciate ligament (PCL): Normal.

COLLATERAL LIGAMENTS & POSTEROLATERAL CORNER:
Medial collateral ligament (MCL): Normal.
Lateral collateral ligament (LCL) complex: Normal.
Posterolateral corner structures: Normal.

EXTENSOR MECHANISM:
Distal quadriceps tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Patella tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Medial patellofemoral ligament (MPFL) and patellar retinacula: Normal.
Patellofemoral tracking: No edema in superolateral Hoffa's fat pad. No lateral patellar tilt or translation. No patella alta. Normal patellar and trochlear morphology. Normal tibial tubercle-trochlear groove (TT-TG) distance measuring 9 mm.

MUSCLES/TENDONS:
No acute muscle strain or muscle atrophy. Visualized tendons not previously discussed are intact without tendinosis or tear.

SOFT TISSUES:
No soft tissue mass. Normal popliteal neurovascular bundle.

IMPRESSION:
1. Resolving osseous contusions at the posterior lateral tibial plateau and periphery of the medial and lateral femoral condyle.
2. Complete, subacute tear of the anterior cruciate ligament.
3. Horizontal tear of the posterior body and posterior horn of the lateral meniscus.
4. Lateral compartment chondrosis.
5. Moderate joint effusion with focal nodular synovial proliferation at the anterior joint line.

In the medial compartment, there are complex tear (main horizontal and radial components) at the body and posterior horn of the medial meniscus. There is displaced meniscal flap into the medial gutter. There is focal grade II chondrosis (less than 50% thickness cartilage loss) at the posteromedial tibial plateau and corresponding posterior weight-baring medial femoral condyle (about 1.4*1.3 cm). 
  
 The lateral compartment, there is longitudinal vertical tear at the posterior horn of the lateral meniscus. There is focal grade II chondral injury at mid weight-baring lateral femoral condyle and posterolateral tibial plateau (about 1.5*1.5 cm).  
  
 The patellofemoral joint, the patellar and trochlear cartilage appears congruent without chondral lesion. The medial patellofemoral ligament is intact.  
  
 In the intercondylar notch, there is chronic complete tear with ligamentous resorption of the anterior cruciate ligament. The posterior cruciate ligament is intact. There is no tibial translation. 
  
 The medial collateral ligament complexes are intact. The posteromedial oblique ligament is intact.  
  
 There is suspected chronic partial tear of the lateral collateral ligament, at mid substance. The popliteofibular ligament is intact. The meniscopopliteal fascicles are intact.  
 The extensor mechanism is normal. 
   
 No knee effusion is present. The surrounding musculature is normal.   -- Focal grade II chondrosis at the posteromedial tibial plateau and corresponding posterior weight-baring medial femoral condyle (about 1.4*1.3 cm), left knee. 
 -- Focal grade II chondral injury at mid weight-baring lateral femoral condyle and posterolateral tibial plateau (about 1.5*1.5 cm).  
 -- Complex tear (main horizontal and radial components) at the body and posterior horn of the medial meniscus. (note: displaced meniscal flap into the medial gutter).  
 -- Longitudinal vertical tear at the posterior horn of the lateral meniscus. 
 -- Chronic complete tear with ligamentous resorption of the anterior cruciate ligament. 
 -- Suspected chronic partial tear of the lateral collateral ligament, at mid substance.

Hallazgos:
No hay alteraciones de señal significativas de la médula ósea.
Ligamentos cruzados y colaterales dentro de límites normales.
Meniscos de morfología y señal conservada, sin criterios categóricos de rotura.
Cartílagos del compartimento femorotibial lateral sin alteraciones. Condropatía superficial de la
zona de carga del compartimento femorotibial medial y patelofemoral.
No hay significativo derrame articular ni quistes poplíteos.
Tendones cuadricipital, rotuliano, tendones de la pata de ganso, bíceps femoral y banda iliotibial
dentro de límites normales.
Trofismo muscular conservado.
Impresión:
Condropatía superficial de la zona de carga del compartimento femorotibial y patelofemoral

Exam Type: MRI KNEE RIGHT WO CONTRAST
Exam Date and Time: [DATE] [TIME]
Indication: Gym injury one week prior.
Comparison: [REDACTED].

TECHNIQUE:
MRI of the right knee was performed on a 1.5 Tesla system with a dedicated knee coil in three planes (axial, sagittal, and coronal), using a standard non-contrast protocol.

FINDINGS:
OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:
Femorotibial alignment is anatomic. Avulsive fragmentation of inferior patellar enthesophytes with some reactive marrow edema in the inferior patella. Background marrow signal is normal without infiltrative marrow process. No aggressive osseous lesions.

JOINT SPACE:
Small joint effusion. No intra-articular bodies. No Baker's cyst.

MEDIAL COMPARTMENT:
Medial meniscus: Normal in morphology and signal.
Medial compartment cartilage: No focal cartilage defects.

LATERAL COMPARTMENT:
Lateral meniscus: Normal in morphology and signal.
Lateral compartment cartilage: No focal cartilage defects.

PATELLOFEMORAL COMPARTMENT:
Patellofemoral compartment cartilage: No focal cartilage defects.

CRUCIATE LIGAMENTS:
Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL): Normal with both bundles intact.
Posterior cruciate ligament (PCL): Normal.

COLLATERAL LIGAMENTS & POSTEROLATERAL CORNER:
Medial collateral ligament (MCL): Normal.
Lateral collateral ligament (LCL) complex: Normal.
Posterolateral corner structures: Normal.

EXTENSOR MECHANISM:
Distal quadriceps tendon: Irregularity of the distal quadriceps tendon, most likely sequelae of laxity due to patella alta, possibly with some mild underlying tendinosis.
Patella tendon: Complete rupture of the proximal patellar tendon with 1.5-2 cm retracted tendon gap and intervening fluid/hematoma formation. Underlying severe patellar tendinosis. Osseous fragments are embedded within the retracted patellar tendon fibers.
Medial patellofemoral ligament (MPFL) and patellar retinacula: Normal.
Patellofemoral tracking: Posttraumatic edema in Hoffa's fat pad. No lateral patellar tilt or translation. Significant patella alta due to the patellar tendon rupture. Normal patellar and trochlear morphology. Normal tibial tubercle-trochlear groove (TT-TG) distance measuring 15 mm.

MUSCLES/TENDONS:
Grade 1 strain of the distal vastus lateralis. Visualized tendons not previously discussed are intact without tendinosis or tear.

SOFT TISSUES:
Extensive posttraumatic soft tissue edema about the knee with moderate prepatellar bursitis. No soft tissue mass. Normal popliteal neurovascular bundle.

IMPRESSION:
1.	Complete, retracted rupture of the proximal patellar tendon with associated avulsive fragmentation of inferior patellar enthesophytes.
2.	Extensive posttraumatic soft tissue about the knee with moderate prepatellar bursitis.

Exam Type: MRI KNEE RIGHT WO CONTRAST
Exam Date and Time: [DATE] [TIME]
Indication: [REDACTED].
Comparison: No relevant prior studies available for comparison.

TECHNIQUE:
MRI of the right knee was performed on a 1.5 Tesla system with a dedicated knee coil in three planes (axial, sagittal, and coronal), using a standard non-contrast protocol.

FINDINGS:
OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:
Alignment is anatomic. No acute fracture. Subentheseal bone marrow edema of the tibial tubercle. Background marrow signal is otherwise normal without infiltrative marrow process. No aggressive osseous lesions.

JOINT SPACE:
Trace joint effusion. No intra-articular bodies. Trace Baker's cyst.

MEDIAL COMPARTMENT:
Medial meniscus: Normal in morphology and signal.
Medial compartment cartilage: Low-grade partial-thickness chondrosis along the weightbearing medial femoral condyle near the intercondylar notch.

LATERAL COMPARTMENT:
Lateral meniscus: Normal in morphology and signal.
Lateral compartment cartilage: No focal cartilage defects.

PATELLOFEMORAL COMPARTMENT:
Patellofemoral compartment cartilage: Focal full-thickness fissuring at the medial patellar facet. Low-grade cartilage fissuring at the median ridge and lateral facet.

CRUCIATE LIGAMENTS:
Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL): Normal with both bundles intact.
Posterior cruciate ligament (PCL): Normal.

COLLATERAL LIGAMENTS & POSTEROLATERAL CORNER:
Medial collateral ligament (MCL): Normal.
Lateral collateral ligament (LCL) complex: Normal.
Posterolateral corner structures: Normal.

EXTENSOR MECHANISM:
Distal quadriceps tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Patella tendon: Moderate distal patellar tendinosis with low-grade interstitial tearing at the insertion, with subenthesial  bone marrow edema in the tibial tubercle.
Medial patellofemoral ligament (MPFL) and patellar retinacula: Normal.
Patellofemoral tracking: No edema in superolateral Hoffa's fat pad. No lateral patellar tilt or translation. No patella alta. Normal patellar and trochlear morphology. Normal tibial tubercle-trochlear groove (TT-TG) distance measuring 11 mm.

MUSCLES/TENDONS:
No acute muscle strain or muscle atrophy. Visualized tendons not previously discussed are intact without tendinosis or tear.

SOFT TISSUES:
Moderate prepatellar soft tissue edema and deep infrapatellar bursitis, likely reactive. No soft tissue mass. Normal popliteal neurovascular bundle.

IMPRESSION:
1.	Moderate distal patellar tendinosis with low-grade interstitial tearing at the insertion, reactive subenthesial bone marrow edema in the tibial tubercle, prepatellar soft tissue swelling, and deep infrapatellar bursitis.

2.	Mild medial and patellofemoral compartmental chondrosis.

Findings:  No significant knee effusion. There is a tiny free edge radial tear of the posterior root of the medial meniscus. An incomplete discoid lateral meniscus is noted. No evidence of tears.  Normal ACL, PCL, MCL and LCL. Normal extensor mechanism.  There is mild thinning and fraying of the medial compartment articular cartilage. The lateral tibiofemoral compartment is well maintained. Normal patellofemoral articulation. Normal visualized bones and surrounding soft tissues.  
Conclusion: Tiny free edge radial tear of the posterior root of the medial meniscus. Mild medial compartment degeneration. No other significant abnormality.

Antecedentes Clínicos:
Gonalgia derecha.
Hallazgos:
No hay alteraciones de señal significativas de la médula ósea.
Ligamentos cruzados y colaterales dentro de límites normales.
Menisco medial de morfología y señal conservada, sin signos de rotura.
Rotura de predominio marginal del cuerno posterior del menisco lateral con mínima extrusión. La
línea úlceras condrales de espesor parcial y total del aspecto posterior de carga del
compartimento femorotibial lateral sin cambios óseos secundarios. Cartílagos del compartimento
femorotibial medial sin alteraciones. Úlceras condrales de espesor total de distribución difusa de la
tróclea femoral. Úlceras condral de espesor parcial de la faceta lateral de la rótula.
Leve derrame articular con discreta sinovitis. No hay quistes poplíteos.
Aumento de señal de la inserción distal del tendón cuadricipital y de la inserción proximal del
tendón rotuliano, sin signos de rotura.
Tendones de la pata de ganso, bíceps femoral y banda iliotibial dentro de límites normales.
Impresión:
Rotura de predominio marginal del cuerno posterior del menisco lateral.
Condropatía con lesiones focales grado 3 del aspecto posterior de la zona de carga del
compartimento femorotibial lateral.
Condropatía lesiones grado 2 y 3 de la tróclea femoral. Condropatía rotuliana con lesiones grado
2.
Leve derrame articular.
Discreta tendinosis rotuliana proximal y cuadricipital distal

COMPARISON:None.

CLINICAL HISTORY:Clinical joint synovitis. Tender medial joint space.

PROCEDURE:Multisequence, multiplanar unenhanced MRI of the right knee according to routine protocol.

IMAGING FINDINGS:

Nondiagnostic scout localizing images reviewed.

Inferiorly surfacing incomplete tear posterior horn medial meniscus extending into the body, which is only minimally peripherally extruded. The posterior root and anterior horn are intact. The lateral meniscus is intact.

Mild intrasubstance ganglion formation proximal fibers of the anterior cruciate ligament compatible with an old, low-grade partial-thickness tear. The posterior cruciate ligament is intact. No tibial translation.

The medial collateral ligament and posterior oblique ligament are intact.

The fibular collateral ligament, popliteus and biceps femoris tendon attachments, and iliotibial band are intact.

No patellofemoral subluxation. No femoral trochlear dysplasia. The TT-TG distance measures 6 mm, within normal limits. The quadriceps and patellar tendons are intact.

Scattered foci of mild chondrosis of the patellofemoral compartment. Small, thin medial plica without infiltration into the patellofemoral compartment. Subtle thinning of articular cartilage involving the posterior weightbearing aspect of the medial femorotibial compartment. Scattered foci of mild chondrosis throughout the lateral femorotibial compartment.

Trace knee joint fluid. Regional musculature is within normal limits. No suspicious focal marrow signal alteration.

IMPRESSION:
1. Inferiorly surfacing oblique tear posterior horn medial meniscus extending into the body, with only slight medial meniscal extrusion.
2. Mild to moderate chondrosis most pronounced along the medial femorotibial compartment, suggesting evolving mild osteoarthritis of the right knee.
3. Old, low-grade partial-thickness tear of the anterior cruciate ligament.
